lesson_title: Why Your Kettle Is an Energy Monster
hook_text: Your kettle uses energy more than two hundred times faster than an LED light. Here is why.
clip_script: Flip over your kettle and find the little label. It says something like 2 000 W. That is its power rating: it transfers 2 000 joules of energy every single second. Now look at an LED bulb: about 9 W. The kettle uses energy more than two hundred times faster. Power is how fast energy moves, and one watt is one joule per second. Because watts are small, we count them in thousands: 1 000 watts is one kilowatt, so the kettle is 2 kilowatts. The biggest users in your home all make heat: the kettle, the stove, the heater and the geyser. Heating water takes a lot of energy, fast. And here is a bonus: power equals voltage times current, so that 2 000 watt kettle on 230 volts pulls almost 9 amperes from the wall.
visual_style: Close-ups of appliance labels; a stopwatch beside a glowing kettle element and a tiny LED; bars growing for each appliance from charger to geyser.
pacing: Quick label reveal, a comparison beat, a fast lineup of appliances, a short formula close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson, then find the power label on three appliances at home.
